Connected original flight/environment/lifecycle contracts. BYTEBB9 is FF for normal control but 1 after celestial-body transfer; nonnegative state halves speed/control accumulators and steps rotation0 by6 modulo4096 untilzero, then writesFF. BYTEBBA is cleared by contact collection each frame, receives2 on structure exit or FF/FE on orientation-dependent entry; mouse/player control consumers bypass free flight and force original poses. BYTEBBB enables resuming interruptedgame: gameplay start and successful load set, gameover/viewer/loadstart clear; E3D4 tests it before resuming. Not a pointer-serialization flag. BYTEBB5 is modulo4 divider used solely by nearby Solice update to decrement angle once per4calls, initialized3 on world/newgame. BYTEBB7 is world atmosphere flag: indexed16-byte table37B58 selects FF/0 and eventmessages11/10 say Atmosphere/NoAtmosphere Detected; surface type145 disc overlay also checks it. Unknown higher selector domains and original sideeffects retained. Rotation2 event spin uses signed WORD39CDA (64steps, negativeinactive) and restore WORD39CDC; expiry restores angle and writesFFFF. These static contracts explain original byte states, not new runtime scenarios, universal physical time or all-entry validity.

Native LEAs, exact18-byte copies (four LONGs plus one WORD), signed row dot-products and the builder/transposer establish that same record structure for these two source-backed mutable buffers. Create canonical source owners then bind the existing type through normal element commands. No runtime-only numeric-overlap alias, guessed pointer scan or per-instruction register seed. Original2B1E calls the three-angle builder then swaps WORD offsets2/6,4/12,10/14 using D0 and saves/restores D0/A5: literal in-place transpose. It is not a proof quantized matrices form an exact inverse or every input is orthogonal. Original29BA reads three model rotations, handles its zero-angle/non-type30 shortcut and otherwise combines original built/view matrix values; its output feeds model_view_matrix. Preserve all sign choices, fixed-point ASL2/SWAP truncation and overflow, original caller assumptions and type30 branch. Source buffers remain mutable original image data; no changed initialization, relocation or all-caller/lifetime guarantee. Nearby duplicate WORD11E initializations remain unnamed: inspected accepted paths provide no demonstrated cache reader, and absent native direct readers do not prove dead storage or an original bug.

Spire WORD28 is a rotation-step phase: adds to rotation1, rises by4 until exactly240 then horizontal offsets90/62 wrap, signed velocityY rises by4 until exactly66 and clears; the zero-velocity path reduces rotation step by4 and at zero installs velocityY=-62 and decrements BYTE1F durability marker. Equality of marker and current durability skips collapse; no normalization or initial-marker invariant is invented. Converter BYTE1F is the signed variant ping-pong step only on durability<=2; zero sets+1 and17 sets-1. Durability>2 instead decrements BYTE3 in D0, returns without committing when that result is zero, and otherwise stores it; at17 follows guarded zero-terminated LONG3C links and sets BYTE28 on linked records. Keep linked pointees unknown and LONG sentinels intact. Door durability6 forces variant0; otherwise variant increments until9, without inferring open/closed geometry or collision state. MiniRocket negative space flag takes the shared link/free-motion body; otherwise WORD24 counts down nonzero delay updates while zeroing velocityY. At zero, rotation1+=16, velocityY-=2 and signed velocityY integrates into worldY. Preserve wrap, exact signed branches, valid original handler/index/record and normal-stack assumptions; no new live encounter or all-path proof.

Two tractor-marker acquisition branches construct records from the original configured WORD at36894 (initial95). Existing type95 near/distant callbacks already use World orientation/variant/scale fields. Producer-local A2 World inputs expose the matching positions, signed velocities and orientation initialization, without claiming the configurable WORD immutable, assigning the No records text as a visual identity, or extending that role to the selected tractor target. Marker shrink behavior and opaque target lifetime remain unchanged. Projector producer3562E iterates exactly eight 10-byte templates36AF6, tagged75..82; acquisition writes the retained tag in D4, scale/variant/rotation and BYTE1F from network state. The common producer receives the existing ProjectorPart role, whose BYTE1F network_animation_step is already consumed by the appropriate original projector callbacks. This does not claim that all eight callbacks animate, that all template presence indices are universally valid, or that every record field is initialized. Original model-specific static placement, branch conditions and all pointer lifetimes remain unchanged. Saved-nearby restoration, non-model particle constructors and Pirate theft alias reads retain their narrower current views.
